output.brief: The slip was mainly self-inflicted, not Halden's doing. Callerby moved its tower crane to the Kestrel warehouse from October 2025 to March 2026. The plant ledger shows the transfer was approved by the regional office, with no transfer forms, and the site superintendent confirms the frame crew went too. The RFI audit trail shows the architect answered 62 of 64 RFIs within the contract period. Most of the 41 "late" RFIs sat in Callerby's own draft status for 9 to 47 days. The draft claim therefore should not go to Halden on 1 December as written; it would be contradicted by Callerby's own records. Design change CO-09 probably contributed, but how much is unresolved. Next steps: commission an independent forensic delay analysis, preferably from someone not already paid on a success fee, and review the crane decision with the regional office. Do not discipline the superintendent for answering Halden's question honestly. I am moderately confident in the direction, less so on the size of each share, because I read only two of the fifteen records.
